name: detection and defence industry
owns: the products and programmes on the other side: WAF, RASP, bot management, EDR, SIEM, DLP, zero trust, and what each of them can actually see
why_in_D: A defence is a system with its own behaviour, its own blind spots and its own assumptions. Knowing which control sees what is as consequential as knowing the payload. The same request is invisible to one product and a page to another, and that difference decides which technique is quiet and which is loud.

factors.name: inspection depth of each control
factors.def: what portion of the request each product actually reads
factors.observable: a payload in a region a product does not inspect

factors.name: TLS termination position per product
factors.def: whether the product sees plaintext or must be given keys
factors.observable: an encrypted request passing uninspected

factors.name: decoding layers before matching
factors.def: how many times the payload is decoded before a rule is applied
factors.observable: a double encoded payload passing

factors.name: rule language expressiveness
factors.def: whether rules can express structure or only strings and regex
factors.observable: a structurally invalid request that no rule covers

factors.name: signature versus behaviour detection balance
factors.def: whether the product only matches known patterns
factors.observable: a novel but obviously malicious shape accepted

factors.name: learning mode residue
factors.def: whether the product learned from a period that included the attacker
factors.observable: attacker traffic treated as baseline

factors.name: exclusion list breadth
factors.def: which paths and parameters are excluded from inspection to avoid false positives
factors.observable: an authenticated route entirely uninspected

factors.name: false positive pressure on the defender
factors.def: whether the team is likely to disable a rule rather than tune it
factors.observable: a rule disabled after a production incident

factors.name: request body handling at the edge
factors.def: whether the body is buffered, streamed or truncated before inspection
factors.observable: a body larger than the buffer accepted

factors.name: multipart and nested encoding handling
factors.def: whether the product parses multipart, JSON in multipart, or base64 within
factors.observable: a payload in a nested layer passing

factors.name: RASP coverage of runtime sinks
factors.def: which sink calls are instrumented in process
factors.observable: a sink call not intercepted

factors.name: RASP tamper resistance
factors.def: whether the agent can be disabled or bypassed from application code
factors.observable: instrumentation disabled at runtime

factors.name: bot management signal set
factors.def: which properties distinguish a browser from automation, and which are forgeable
factors.observable: an automated client treated as human

factors.name: javascript challenge solvability
factors.def: whether the challenge requires a real engine or only a script evaluator
factors.observable: a challenge solved outside a real browser

factors.name: behavioural biometrics coverage
factors.def: whether pointer, keystroke and timing patterns are modelled and how they degrade
factors.observable: an automated flow with human like timing passing

factors.name: device fingerprint stability requirement
factors.def: how much a client must stay consistent to be trusted
factors.observable: a session maintained across changing properties

factors.name: reputation and IP class handling
factors.def: which address classes are treated differently
factors.observable: a request treated differently by source class

factors.name: rate limiting granularity in the product
factors.def: what the product counts, and whether counting is per node
factors.observable: an allowance exceeded in aggregate

factors.name: account takeover detection signals
factors.def: which anomalies trigger a challenge or block
factors.observable: a login that should have been challenged

factors.name: credential stuffing detection
factors.def: whether distributed attempts across accounts are correlated
factors.observable: low and slow attempts passing

factors.name: EDR coverage of servers versus endpoints
factors.def: whether the web tier is instrumented at all
factors.observable: a process execution on the web tier with no telemetry

factors.name: command line logging completeness
factors.def: whether the full command including arguments is recorded
factors.observable: a command in the log with arguments truncated

factors.name: script block logging
factors.def: whether interpreted code is captured
factors.observable: executed script absent from logs

factors.name: network telemetry east west coverage
factors.def: whether internal traffic is visible or only the perimeter
factors.observable: an internal connection with no record

factors.name: DNS logging and retention
factors.def: whether queries are recorded and for how long
factors.observable: a lookup absent from the log

factors.name: proxy versus direct egress
factors.def: whether all egress passes an inspection point
factors.observable: a connection that avoided the proxy

factors.name: SIEM rule coverage per technique
factors.def: which techniques have a detection and which have none
factors.observable: a technique with no corresponding rule

factors.name: detection latency
factors.def: the time from action to alert
factors.observable: measured gap between event and alert

factors.name: alert triage capacity
factors.def: whether the team can process the volume the sensor produces
factors.observable: an unprocessed alert queue

factors.name: log source completeness
factors.def: which systems produce logs at all
factors.observable: a system with no logging configured

factors.name: clock synchronisation across sources
factors.def: whether events can be ordered across systems
factors.observable: timestamps that disagree by more than the drift

factors.name: retention versus investigation window
factors.def: whether logs last long enough to investigate an incident found late
factors.observable: a gap in the record where the event was

factors.name: DLP coverage of outbound channels
factors.def: which channels are watched for data leaving
factors.observable: an exfiltration path with no coverage

factors.name: zero trust policy evaluation point
factors.def: where identity and device are evaluated, and whether the evaluation can be reached around
factors.observable: a request served without policy evaluation

factors.name: device posture signal trust
factors.def: whether the posture is asserted by the client or measured by the platform
factors.observable: a posture claimed by an unmanaged device

factors.name: conditional access gap
factors.def: which applications are excluded from the policy
factors.observable: an application reachable without the policy

factors.name: administrative plane protection
factors.def: whether the management interface has the same controls as the data plane
factors.observable: an admin console with weaker authentication

factors.name: honeypot placement and realism
factors.def: whether decoys exist and whether they are convincing
factors.observable: a decoy that reveals itself

factors.name: deception response consistency
factors.def: whether a decoy answers like the real system, since a difference reveals it
factors.observable: a response shape differing from production

factors.name: canary token placement
factors.def: whether tripwires exist in credentials, files and DNS
factors.observable: a used canary with no alert

factors.name: incident response playbook depth
factors.def: whether the playbook covers containment, not only notification
factors.observable: a playbook with no isolation step

factors.name: forensic readiness
factors.def: whether memory and disk can be captured before they change
factors.observable: a capture possible within the stated window

factors.name: containment reversibility
factors.def: whether isolating a host costs the business more than the incident
factors.observable: a containment decision delayed by cost

factors.name: backup isolation
factors.def: whether backups are reachable from the production identity, which decides ransomware impact
factors.observable: a backup deleted by a production credential

factors.name: restore time objective
factors.def: how long a restore actually takes, measured rather than stated
factors.observable: measured restore duration

factors.name: purple team validation coverage
factors.def: which detections were tested against a real technique rather than assumed
factors.observable: a detection that never fired in a test

factors.name: detection bias toward the tool vendor
factors.def: whether the detection set covers only what the deployed product emits
factors.observable: a technique visible only in logs the product does not read

factors.name: cloud control plane logging
factors.def: whether API calls in the cloud account are recorded
factors.observable: a permission change with no record

factors.name: identity provider log export
factors.def: whether authentication events leave the provider and reach the SIEM
factors.observable: a failed login burst absent centrally

factors.name: third party access logging
factors.def: whether supplier sessions are recorded like employee sessions
factors.observable: a vendor action missing from the audit trail

factors.name: alert fatigue effect on judgement
factors.def: whether a real alert is lost among noise, which is a human detection limit
factors.observable: a true positive dismissed as noise

factors.name: assumption that an alert means a human read it
factors.def: whether automated alerting is mistaken for response
factors.observable: an alert with no disposition

factors.name: vendor product false negative marketing
factors.def: whether a coverage claim was measured independently
factors.observable: a claim with no test behind it

factors.name: defence in depth versus single point
factors.def: whether one control failing exposes everything
factors.observable: a bypass of one control leaving no other check

factors.name: control misconfiguration prevalence
factors.def: whether the default configuration is the effective one
factors.observable: a default that disables the feature

factors.name: security product supply chain risk
factors.def: whether the defence product itself is a dependency with update rights
factors.observable: a control with an auto update channel

factors.name: certificate and key management
factors.def: where the inspection keys live and who can use them
factors.observable: a key usable by an operator without approval

factors.name: break glass versus policy
factors.def: whether the emergency path bypasses the controls it is protecting
factors.observable: an emergency access route with weaker checks

factors.name: measurement of defence effectiveness
factors.def: whether anyone measures whether the control catches anything
factors.observable: a detection rate over time

factors.name: cost of the control versus the risk
factors.def: whether the control costs more than the loss it prevents
factors.observable: an economically irrational control in place

factors.name: regulatory acceptance of the control
factors.def: whether an auditor accepts this control as satisfying a requirement
factors.observable: a control rejected during assessment

factors.name: detection evasion by living off the platform
factors.def: whether the technique uses only legitimate features, which no signature describes
factors.observable: an action composed of allowed operations only

factors.name: telemetry blind spot at the edge of ownership
factors.def: which boundary has no owner and therefore no logging
factors.observable: a hop between two systems with no record

factors.name: response authority at the edge
factors.def: who can block traffic and how quickly, which decides whether detection becomes prevention
factors.observable: time from decision to block
